findings.title: Invalidate connected calendars after deleting the cache
findings.body: The cache-deletion success handler only calls the optional onSuccess callback; it never invalidates the connectedCalendars query that supplies cacheUpdatedAt. The wrapper forwards an optional onChanged callback and disables refetchOnWindowFocus, so without a caller-provided refetch the UI continues displaying the deleted cache's timestamp and deletion action after reporting success. Invalidate connectedCalendars here, as the disconnect mutation already does.

findings.title: Resolve cache status for in-memory delegation credentials
findings.body: Connected calendars can contain in-memory delegation credentials with negative IDs, whereas CalendarCache rows reference persisted credentials. Looking up status solely by the displayed credentialId therefore returns no cache for these connections, even when availability is being served from cached data. CalendarCacheRepository.getCachedAvailability explicitly handles this case through userId and the calendar key, including reuse of pre-delegation cache rows. Resolve the corresponding persisted cache records for delegated connections as well; otherwise these users cannot see or clear their active cache through the new UI.

findings.title: Resolve the environment file relative to the script location
findings.body: ENV_FILE is relative to the caller's working directory, not the script directory. Running bash scripts/test-gcal-webhooks.sh from the repository root writes ../.env outside the repository, creating it if necessary, while leaving the application's environment unchanged. Derive the repository root from BASH_SOURCE before selecting .env so the advertised webhook configuration is actually applied.

findings.title: Make the environment update work with GNU sed
findings.body: The sed -i '' invocation uses BSD/macOS syntax and fails under GNU sed on Linux. When GOOGLE_WEBHOOK_URL already exists, the script consequently leaves the old URL in place but still prints that it updated the file successfully. Use a portable replacement strategy or distinguish the sed implementations, and check the command result before reporting success.
